questions.question: Why ask a coding assistant for a plan before it writes code for a larger change?
options: Models cannot write code without a plan
Reviewing a short plan catches wrong assumptions before hundreds of lines are built on them
Plans make the final code run faster
It reduces the number of tests needed
questions.explanation: A plan is quick to review and lets you correct the approach before code is written.

questions.question: What is the best way to ask for help with a failing test?
options: Paste only the last line of the error
Ask for a try/except around the failing line
Paste the full error and stack trace, the relevant code, what you expected, and ask for the root cause first
questions.explanation: Full context lets the model diagnose the real cause instead of patching over the symptom.

questions.question: Which pattern in generated code is a security problem?
options: Building SQL by inserting user input into the query string
Using a parameterised query with placeholders
questions.explanation: String-built SQL with user input enables SQL injection; parameterised queries avoid it.

questions.question: Why should you read the tests a model generates, not just run them?
options: Tests are not needed if the code compiles
Tests written by the same model can share the same misunderstanding as the code
Reading tests is required by pytest
questions.explanation: If the model misunderstood the requirement, both code and tests may encode the same mistake and still pass.
